chain.label: Deteriorated elevator trim tab locknut inserts
chain.trigger: the trim tab attachment screws' locknut inserts...showed evidence of age and reuse

chain.label: Undocumented, unengineered, untested airplane modifications
chain.trigger: the airplane had undergone many structural and flight control modifications that were undocumented and for which no flight testing or analysis had been performed

chain.label: Pilot raced airplane without adequate flight testing of its modified envelope
chain.trigger: the pilot's operation of the airplane in the unique air racing environment without adequate flight testing

caused_by.evidence: it is likely that, had engineering evaluations and diligent flight testing for the modifications been performed, many of the airplane's undesirable structural and control characteristics could have been identified and corrected

chain.label: Trim tab attachment screws went loose and one developed an undetected fatigue crack
chain.trigger: the loosening of the trim tab attachment screws and the deteriorated condition of the locknut inserts should have been noticeable to the ground crew

caused_by.evidence: the deteriorated locknuts, therefore, resulted in loose elevator trim tab attachment screws and fatigue cracking in one screw

chain.label: Aerodynamic flutter of elevator trim tabs at racing speed
chain.trigger: the decreased stiffness was sufficient to allow aerodynamic flutter of the elevator trim tabs

caused_by.evidence: the looseness of the attachment screws and the fatigue crack in one of the screws would have allowed for reduced stiffness of the trim tab system that could have allowed a flutter condition to develop
the addition of filler material to the elevator trim tabs (which increased their weight and moved their CG aft) also increased the potential for flutter

chain.label: Left elevator trim tab link assembly buckled and fractured
chain.trigger: dynamic compressive loads in the left elevator trim tab's link assembly that increased beyond its buckling strength, causing a bending fracture

caused_by.evidence: excitation of the flutter resulted in dynamic compressive loads in the left elevator trim tab's link assembly that increased beyond its buckling strength, causing a bending fracture

chain.label: Left roll upset and high-G pitch-up (vertical acceleration peaked at 17.3 G)
chain.trigger: the airplane rolled from its established approximate 73°-left-bank turn to about 93° left bank in less than 1 second; vertical acceleration peaked at 17.3 G

caused_by.evidence: the loss of the left trim tab's downward force on the elevator resulted in a concurrent sudden upward deflection of the elevator, a sudden and forceful aft movement of the control stick, the pitch-up of the airplane, and the rapid increase in G
had the airplane retained its original, redundant tab design, the pilot may have been able to maintain some control following a failure in only one tab

chain.label: Pilot rendered completely incapacitated by G-LOC
chain.trigger: the pilot's time of useful consciousness was likely less than 1 second...the pilot soon became completely incapacitated

caused_by.evidence: both the rate of G onset and the high-G level exceeded human tolerance...the pilot's time of useful consciousness was likely less than 1 second

chain.label: Uncontrolled climb and helical descent into airport ramp/spectator box seating area
chain.trigger: collided with the airport ramp in the spectator box seating area following a loss of control

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's continued climb and helical descent occurred without his control

chain.label: Pilot and 10 people on the ground killed; at least 64 injured
chain.trigger: The pilot and 10 people on the ground sustained fatal injuries, and at least 64 people on the ground were injured

caused_by.evidence: the airplane sustained substantial damage, fragmenting upon collision with the ramp
